{{History of art sidebar}}
{{Indian art}}'''Indian art''' consists of a variety of art forms, including [[Indian painting|painting]], [[sculpture in the Indian subcontinent|sculpture]], [[Indian pottery|pottery]], and [[textile arts]] such as [[Silk in the Indian subcontinent#Origin|woven silk]]. Geographically, it spans [[South Asia]], including what is now [[India]], [[Pakistan]], [[Bangladesh]], [[Sri Lanka]], [[Nepal]], [[Bhutan]], and at times [[Afghanistan]], the [[Maldives]], and [[Tibet]], amongst a few other places. A strong sense of design is characteristic of Indian art and can be observed in its modern and traditional forms.

The earliest Indian art originated during the prehistoric settlements of the 3rd millennium BCE, such as the rock shelters of [[Bhimbetka]], which contain some of the world's oldest known cave paintings.{{cn|date=November 2025}} On its way to modern times, Indian art has had cultural influences, as well as religious influences such as [[Hindu art|Hinduism]], [[Buddhist art|Buddhism]], [[Jain art|Jainism]], [[Sikh art and culture|Sikhism]] and [[Islam in India#Indo-Islamic art and architecture|Islam]]. In spite of this complex mixture of religious traditions, generally, the prevailing artistic style at any time and place has been shared by the major religious groups.

In historic art, sculpture in stone and metal, mainly religious, has survived the Indian climate better than other media and provides most of the best remains. Many of the most important ancient finds that are not in carved stone come from the surrounding, drier regions rather than India itself. [[Indian funeral]] and philosophic traditions exclude [[grave goods]], which is the main source of ancient art in other cultures.

Indian artist styles historically followed [[Indian religion]]s out of the subcontinent, having an especially large influence in Tibet, [[South East Asia|Southeast Asia]] and [[China]]. Indian art has itself received influences at times, especially from [[Central Asia]], [[Iran]], and [[Europe]].

'''Organopalladium chemistry''' is a branch of [[organometallic chemistry]] that deals with organic [[palladium]] compounds and their reactions. Palladium is often used as a catalyst in the reduction of [[alkene]]s and [[alkyne]]s with [[hydrogen]]. This process involves the formation of a palladium-carbon [[covalent bond]]. Palladium is also prominent in carbon-carbon [[coupling reaction]]s, as demonstrated in [[tandem reaction]]s.<ref>''Handbook of Organopalladium Chemistry for Organic Synthesis'' Ei-Negishi John Wiley (2002) {{ISBN|0-471-31506-0}}</ref>

{{Short description|Molecular-structure relationship}}
In [[chemistry]] the [[Descriptor (Chemistry)|descriptor]] '''vicinal''' (from [[Latin]] ''vicinus'' = neighbor), abbreviated ''vic'', is a [[descriptor (chemistry)|descriptor]] that identifies two [[functional group]]s as bonded to two adjacent [[carbon]] atoms (i.e., in a 1,2-relationship).  It may arise from [[vicinal difunctionalization]].

{{Short description|Genre of literature common in the ancient Near East}}
[[File:Lens - Inauguration du Louvre-Lens le 4 décembre 2012, la Galerie du Temps, n° 018.JPG|thumb|right|Tablet of the ''[[Dialogue between a Man and His God]]'', {{circa|19th}}–17th centuries BC, [[Louvre]]]]
'''Wisdom literature''' is a [[Literary genre|genre of literature]] common in the [[ancient Near East]]. It consists of statements by [[sage (philosophy)|sages]] and the [[Wisdom|wise]] that offer teachings about [[divinity]] and [[virtue]]. Although this genre uses techniques of traditional [[oral storytelling]], it was disseminated in written form.

The earliest known wisdom literature dates back to the middle of the 3rd millennium BC, originating from ancient [[Mesopotamia]] and [[Ancient Egypt|Egypt]]. These regions continued to produce wisdom literature over the subsequent two and a half millennia. Wisdom literature from Greek, Chinese, and Indian cultures started appearing around the middle of the 1st millennium BC. In the 1st millennium AD, Egyptian-Greek wisdom literature emerged, some elements of which were later incorporated into Islamic thought.

Much of wisdom literature can be broadly categorized into two types – conservative "positive wisdom" and critical "negative wisdom" or "vanity literature":<ref name="Samet2020"/><ref name="Clarke2019">
{{cite book |last1=Clarke |first1=Michael |title=Achilles Beside Gilgamesh: Mortality and Wisdom in Early Epic Poetry |date=2019 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-1-108-48178-6 |pages=55–56 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=tG3CDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA55}}
</ref><ref name="Hilber2019">
{{cite book |last1=Hilber |first1=John W. |editor1-last=Boda |editor1-first=Mark J. |editor2-last=Meek |editor2-first=Russell L. |editor3-last=Osborne |editor3-first=William R. |title=Riddles and Revelations: Explorations into the Relationship between Wisdom and Prophecy in the Hebrew Bible |date=2019 |publisher=Bloomsbury Publishing |isbn=978-0-567-67165-3 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=k4hoDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA57}}
</ref><ref name="Cohen2013">
{{cite book |last1=Cohen |first1=Yoram |title=Wisdom from the Late Bronze Age |date=2013 |publisher=Society of Biblical Literature |isbn=978-1-58983-754-6 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=VTVXAQAAQBAJ&pg=PA14}}
</ref><ref name="Cohen2021"/>
* Conservative Positive Wisdom – Pragmatic, real-world advice about proper behavior and actions,<ref name="Clarke2019"/> attaining success in life,<ref name="Hilber2019"/><ref name="Cohen2013"/> living a good and fulfilling life,<ref name="Cohen2013"/> etc.. Examples of this genre include: ''[[Book of Proverbs]]'', ''The [[Instructions of Shuruppak]]'', and first part of ''Sima Milka''.<ref name="Cohen2013"/>
* Critical Negative Wisdom (also called "Vanity Literature" or "Wisdom in Protest") – A more [[philosophical pessimism|pessimistic]] outlook, frequently expressing [[philosophical scepticism|skepticism]] about the scope of human achievements, highlighting the inevitability of mortality,<ref name="Clarke2019"/> advocating the rejection of all material gains,<ref name="Cohen2021"/> and expressing the [[carpe diem]] view that, since nothing has intrinsic value (''[[vanitas|vanity theme]]'') and all will come to an end (''[[memento mori]]'' theme), therefore one should just enjoy life to the fullest while they can (''carpe diem theme'').<ref name="Hilber2019"/><ref name="Cohen2013"/> Examples of this genre include: ''Qohelet'' ([[Ecclesiastes]]), ''The Ballad of Early Rulers'', ''Enlil and Namzitarra'', the second part of ''Sima Milka'' (the son's response),<ref name="Cohen2013"/> and ''Nig-Nam Nu-Kal'' ("''Nothing is of Value''").<ref name="Cohen2021"/>

Another common genre is existential works that deal with the relationship between man and God, divine reward and punishment, theodicy, the problem of evil, and why bad things happen to good people. The protagonist is a "just sufferer" – a good person beset by tragedy, who tries to understand his lot in life. The most well known example is the Book of Job, however it was preceded by, and likely based on, earlier Mesopotamian works such as ''The [[Babylonian Theodicy]]'' (sometimes called ''The Babylonian Job''), ''[[Ludlul bēl nēmeqi]]'' ("''I Will Praise the Lord of Wisdom''" or "''The Poem of the Righteous Sufferer''"), ''[[Dialogue between a Man and His God]]'', and the Sumerian ''Man and His God''.<ref name="Cohen2021"/>

The literary genre of [[mirrors for princes]], which has a long history in [[Islamic literature|Islamic]] and Western [[Renaissance literature]], is a secular cognate of wisdom literature. In [[classical antiquity]], the [[didactic]] poetry of [[Hesiod]], particularly his ''[[Works and Days]]'', was regarded as a source of knowledge similar to the wisdom literature of [[Ancient Egypt|Egypt]], [[Babylonia]] and Israel.{{citation needed|date=May 2018}} [[Pre-Islamic poetry]] is replete with many poems of wisdom, including the poetry of [[Zuhayr bin Abi Sulma|Zuhayr bin Abī Sūlmā]] (520–609).

{{short description|Annual awards by the Blues Foundation since 1980}}
[[File:Blues_Foundation_Blues_Trail_Marker.jpg | thumb | right | alt=Blues Foundation Blues Trail Marker | Blues Foundation Blues Trail Marker]]
The '''Blues Music Awards''', formerly known as the '''W. C. Handy Awards''' (or "The Handys"), are [[award]]s presented by the [[Blues Foundation]], a [[non-profit organization]] set up to foster [[blues]] heritage. The awards were originally named in honor of [[W. C. Handy]], "Father of the Blues".<ref>{{Cite web|date=2002-06-02|title=BMI Ain’t Singin’ the Blues with Sweep of Handys|url=https://www.bmi.com/news/entry/20020603_bmi_aint_singin_the_blues_with_sweep_of_handys|access-date=2021-03-04|website=BMI.com|language=en}}</ref> The first award was presented in 1980 and is "universally recognized as the highest accolade afforded musicians and songwriters in blues music".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.offbeat.com/2013/12/10/blues-awards-nominees-announced/ |title=2013 Blues Awards Nominees Announced |website=Offbeat.com |date=December 10, 2013 |access-date=January 9, 2014}}</ref> In 2006, the awards were renamed Blues Music Awards in an effort to increase public appreciation of the significance of the awards.<ref>[http://blues.about.com/od/bluesawards/a/bl2006bmas.htm] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070914044401/http://blues.about.com/od/bluesawards/a/bl2006bmas.htm|date=September 14, 2007}}</ref>

They are presented annually in [[Memphis, Tennessee]], where the Blues Foundation is located, although the 2008 award ceremony was held in [[Tunica, Mississippi]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.blues.org:80/bluesmusicawards/index.php4|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090615201222/http://www.blues.org/bluesmusicawards/index.php4|url-status=dead|title=Blues Foundation :: The Blues Music Awards|archive-date=June 15, 2009|website=Blues.org|access-date=June 26, 2026}}</ref> The 39th Blues Music Awards were held on May 10, 2018, at the [[Memphis Cook Convention Center]]. Two new award categories had been announced (Instrumentalist-Vocals and Blues Rock Artist of the Year) bringing the number of awards to be presented up to 26 in total.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blues.org/2018-blues-music-award-nominees-announced/|title=2018 Blues Music Award nominees announced: Taj Mahal, Mavis Staples, Keb' Mo', N. Mississippi Allstars among nominees. |website=Blues Foundation |access-date=17 April 2018}}</ref> The 40th Blues Music Awards took place on May 9, 2019, with the Historical Album of the Year category being dropped, reducing the overall number of categories to 25.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bmi.com/events/entry/581601|title=2019 Blues Music Awards: Memphis: May 9, 2019 – Calendar|website=Bmi.com|access-date=22 April 2019}}</ref>

The 41st ceremony was scheduled for May 7, 2020, but the live event was cancelled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blues.org/blues-music-awards/|title=The 2020 Blues Music Awards in Memphis, TN are canceled.|website=Blues.org|access-date=March 29, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://blues.org/blues-music-awards/|title=Blues Music  Awards|first=Robin|last=McKay|website=Blues.org|access-date=January 29, 2020}}</ref> The 2020 winners were announced at a [[Virtual meeting|virtual]] event.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://blues.org/blues-music-awards/|title=BLUES MUSIC AWARDS|first=Robin|last=McKay|website=Blues.org|access-date=May 4, 2020}}</ref> The 42nd ceremony was again presented at a virtual event on June 6, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://blues.org/blues-music-awards/|title=BLUES MUSIC AWARDS|first=Robin|last=McKay|website=Blues.org|access-date=April 14, 2021}}</ref> The 43rd ceremony took place on May 5, 2022, as the first in-person event since 2019.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://blues.org/2022-blues-music-awards-winners/|title=2022 Blues Music Awards Winners|website=Blues.org|date=May 6, 2022|access-date=May 29, 2022}}</ref> The 44th event was held on May 11, 2023, in Memphis.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rockandbluesmuse.com/2023/01/10/2023-blues-music-award-nominees-announced/|title=2023 Blues Music Award Nominees Announced|first=Martine|last=Ehrenclou|website=Rockandbluesmuse.com|date=January 10, 2023|access-date=April 19, 2023}}</ref> The 45th event took place  on May 8, 2024, in Memphis,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://blues.org/blues-music-awards-2/|title=Blue Music Awards - Home Page & Nominations|first=Candace|last=Dickerson|website=Blues.org|access-date=February 23, 2024}}</ref> with the 46th event held on May 9, 2025.<ref name="auto2">{{Cite web|url=https://blues.org/2025-blues-music-awards-winners/|title=2025 Blues Music Awards Winners|first=Clare|last=Freeman|website=Blues.org|date=May 14, 2025|access-date=May 20, 2025}}</ref>

The 47th ceremony took place on May 7, 2026, in Memphis, with the addition of a new category (the 26th) – International Blues Album.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://blues.org/blues-music-awards-2/|title=Blue Music Awards- Home Page & Nominations - Blues Foundation|website=Blues.org|access-date=June 26, 2026}}</ref>

'''Video astronomy''' ''(aka - Camera Assisted Astronomy, aka electronically-assisted astronomy or "EAA"<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.space.com/video-astronomy-celestron-rasa-8-telescope-review.html/|title = Video astronomy: Bring the universe to your friends with Celestron's RASA 8 telescope|website = [[Space.com]]|date = 15 July 2020}}</ref>)'' is a branch of astronomy for near real-time observing of relatively faint [[astronomy|astronomical]] objects using very sensitive [[Charge-coupled device|CCD]] or [[CMOS]] cameras. Unlike [[lucky imaging]], video astronomy does not discard unwanted frames, and image corrections such as [[Dark-frame subtraction|dark subtraction]] are often not applied, however, the gathered data may be retained and processed in more traditional ways.. Although the field has a long history reaching back to 1928 with the inception of live television broadcasting of the planet Mars,<ref>{{cite web| url=https://static.wixstatic.com/media/ee9c23_93509155f64547578850b6bd0d601598.jpg/v1/fill/w_885,h_1245,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01/ee9c23_93509155f64547578850b6bd0d601598.jpg | format=JPG | title=Television May Solve Star Secrets | access-date=2023-12-28}}</ref> it has largely been developed more recently by amateur enthusiasts and is characterized by the use of relatively inexpensive equipment, such as easily available sensitive security cameras, in contrast to the equipment used for advanced [[astrophotography]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.stargazing.net/David/astrophoto/index.html|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150914031031/http://www.stargazing.net/David/astrophoto/index.html|url-status=dead|title=Astroimaging - Astronomical Observing with Cameras|archivedate=September 14, 2015|website=www.stargazing.net}}</ref>

By using either method of rapid internally stacked images, or very short exposure times, and using a TV monitor (for analog cameras) or a computer with readily available software (for USB cameras), video astronomy allows observers to see colour and detail that would not register to the eye. Because the image can be displayed on a monitor or [[television]] screen it allows multiple people to share 'live' images; using the internet it is possible for a worldwide audience to share such images. Live broadcasting websites exist for sharing live video astronomy feeds.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nightskiesnetwork.com/ |title=Home |website=nightskiesnetwork.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.videoastronomylive.co.uk |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150214073328/http://www.videoastronomylive.co.uk/ |archive-date=2015-02-14 |title=Video Astronomy Live}}</ref>

Video astronomy, combined with remote control of a telescope, allows anyone including disabled people to operate a telescope remotely, or observers in a [[Light pollution|light-polluted]] area to operate a telescope in another area, even another country.

Other benefits of the highly sensitive cameras used in video astronomy are the ability to see through thin cloud, and the ability to see many faint objects in areas suffering from light pollution.
The equipment used varies from webcams and basic security cameras to specialized video astronomy cameras. Recent growing interest in the video 'near-live' aspect of astronomy has brought about websites devoted purely to the practice <ref>{{cite web |url=http://ballaratman.wix.com/videoastronomy |title = Video Astronomy}}</ref> and forums for users of the equipment <ref>{{cite web |url=http://astrovideoforum.proboards.com/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150927051432/http://astrovideoforum.proboards.com/ |archive-date=2015-09-27 |title=Home {{!}} VIDEO ASTRONOMY}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cloudynights.com/forum/73-electronically-assisted-astronomy/ |title = Electronically Assisted Astronomy (EAA) - Cloudy Nights}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://stargazerslounge.com/forum/123-video-astronomy/ |title = EEVA - Reports - Stargazers Lounge| date=7 August 2023 }}</ref>

{{Short description|Movement in literature}}
'''Literary impressionism''' can be defined as when an author centers their story or attention on the character's mental life such as the character's impressions, feelings, sensations or emotions.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Warodell |first=Johan Adam |title=Conrad's Decentered Fiction |publisher=Cambridge University Press |year=2022 |isbn=9781316512197 |pages=153}}</ref> To broaden the scope of what impressionistic literature is, it can be identified by the following attributes: ambiguous meaning (character motivation, themes, or narration is up to reader interpretation), non-chronological narrative, strategic selection of details (to convey the impressions left by an incident or scene), emotional landscape (a focus on how the events of the scene affect the narrator), and personal point-of-view (a particular character's subjective perception of events).<ref>{{Cite web |title=How to Write Literary Impressionism: History and Tips for Impressionistic Writing - 2026 |url=https://www.masterclass.com/articles/how-to-write-literary-impressionism |access-date=2026-02-23 |website=MasterClass |language=en}}</ref> With personal point-of-view the edges of reality are blurred by choosing points of view that lie outside the norm, which is reminiscent of the Impressionist art movement and Monet's blurry style.<ref name="Baldick">{{cite encyclopedia |surname=Baldick |given=Chris |authorlink=Chris Baldick |entry=Impressionism |title=The Oxford Dictionary of Literary Terms |edition=4th |format=Online Version |year=2015 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=9780191783234 |entry-url= https://www.oxfordreference.com/display/10.1093/acref/9780198715443.001.0001/acref-9780198715443-e-587?rskey=MsgKuo&result=596 |url=https://www.oxfordreference.com/display/10.1093/acref/9780198715443.001.0001/acref-9780198715443 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

{{Short description|Study of compounds containing a boron-carbon bond}}
[[File:OrganoboronLogo.svg|right|thumb|150x150px|Organoboron]]
'''Organoboron chemistry''' or '''organoborane chemistry''' studies '''organoboron compounds''', also called '''organoboranes'''.  These [[chemical compounds]] combine [[boron]] and [[carbon]]; typically, they are [[Organic compound|organic]] derivatives of [[borane]] (BH<sub>3</sub>), as in the trialkyl boranes.<ref name="susan" /><ref name="christoph" />

Organoboranes and -borates enable many [[Chemical transformation|chemical transformations]] in [[organic chemistry]] — most importantly, [[hydroboration]] and [[carboboration]].  Most reactions transfer a [[Nucleophile|nucleophilic]] boron substituent to an [[Electrophile|electrophilic center]] either inter- or [[Intramolecular reaction|intramolecularly]].  In particular, [[Locant|α,β]]-unsaturated borates and borates with an α leaving group are highly susceptible to intramolecular 1,2-migration of a group from boron to the electrophilic α position. Oxidation or [[protonolysis]] of the resulting organoboranes generates many organic products, including alcohols, carbonyl compounds, alkenes, and halides.<ref name=NI />

{{Short description|Sub-branch of human geography}}
{{Geography sidebar}}{{History of geography sidebar}}[[File:Plan de Paris 1740 BNF07710703.jpg|thumb|right|250px|A 1740 map of [[Paris]].]]
[[File:Theatrum Orbis Terrarum, by Abraham Ortelius, World, 1572.jpg|thumb|Ortelius World Map, 1570]]

'''Historical geography''' is the branch of [[geography]] that studies the ways in which geographic phenomena have changed over time.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Sauer |first=Carl O. |date=1941 |title=Foreword to Historical Geography |url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/00045604109357211 |journal=Annals of the Association of American Geographers |language=en |volume=31 |issue=1 |pages=1–24 |doi=10.1080/00045604109357211 |issn=0004-5608|url-access=subscription }}</ref> In its modern form, it is a synthesizing discipline which shares both topical and methodological similarities with [[history]], [[anthropology]], [[ecology]], [[geology]], [[environmental studies]], [[literary studies]], and other fields.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Harris |first=Cole |date=1991 |title=Power, Modernity, and Historical Geography |url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.1467-8306.1991.tb01714.x |journal=Annals of the Association of American Geographers |language=en |volume=81 |issue=4 |pages=671–683 |doi=10.1111/j.1467-8306.1991.tb01714.x |issn=0004-5608|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Pounds |first=Norman J. G. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Zgc5AAAAIAAJ&dq=historical+geography&pg=PR7 |title=An Historical Geography of Europe |date=1990-08-31 |publisher=CUP Archive |isbn=978-0-521-32217-1 |language=en}}</ref> Although the majority of work in historical geography is considered [[human geography]], the field also encompasses studies of geographic change which are not primarily [[Human impact on the environment|anthropogenic]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Taxel |first=Itamar |date=2023-03-04 |title=Towards an Integration of Historical Trees into the Mediterranean Archaeological Record: Case Studies from Central Israel |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/14614103.2021.1877512 |journal=Environmental Archaeology |language=en |volume=28 |issue=2 |pages=86–109 |doi=10.1080/14614103.2021.1877512 |issn=1461-4103|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Historical geography is often a major component of school and university curricula in geography and [[social studies]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Keighren |first1=Innes M. |last2=Crampton |first2=Jeremy W. |last3=Ginn |first3=Franklin |last4=Kirsch |first4=Scott |last5=Kobayashi |first5=Audrey |last6=Naylor |first6=Simon N |last7=Seemann |first7=Jörn |date=2017 |title=Teaching the history of geography: Current challenges and future directions |url=http://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/0309132515575940 |journal=Progress in Human Geography |language=en |volume=41 |issue=2 |pages=245–262 |doi=10.1177/0309132515575940 |issn=0309-1325|hdl=1983/9604b2ca-adf3-412b-8d8e-d945c1802cd1 |hdl-access=free |url-access=subscription }}</ref> Current research in historical geography is being performed by scholars in more than forty countries.<ref>Powell, Richard, and Robert M Wilson. [https://ejournals.unm.edu/index.php/historicalgeography/article/view/3481/xhtml "What Futures for the Pillar of Geography? a Report on the 16th International Conference of Historical Geographers, London."] ''Historical Geography'' 43 (2015).</ref>

{{short description|Compound that is derived from a similar compound by a chemical reaction}}
In [[chemistry]], a '''derivative''' is a [[Chemical compound|compound]] that is [[wikt:derive#Verb|derived]] from a similar compound by a [[chemical reaction]], or that ''can be imagined to'' arise from another compound, if one [[atom]] or [[functional group|group of atoms]] is replaced with another atom or group of atoms.<ref name=chemicool>{{cite web
 |title = Definition of Derivative
 |publisher = Chemicool
 |date = 2007-09-18
 |url = http://www.chemicool.com/definition/derivative.html
 |access-date = 2007-09-18
 |archive-date = 2021-08-31
 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20210831142000/https://www.chemicool.com/definition/derivative.html
 |url-status = live
 }}</ref>{{bettersource|date=October 2025}} The exact definition of "derivative" depends on the specific context.<ref>{{cite book|title=Forensic Chemistry of Substance Misuse |chapter=What is a Derivative? |date=2022 |pages=153–161 |doi=10.1039/9781839166631-00153 |isbn=978-1-83916-450-7 }}</ref>

The related term [[structural analogue]] is common in [[organic chemistry]].

In [[biochemistry]], the word is used for compounds that at least theoretically can be formed from the [[precursor (chemistry)|precursor]] compound.<ref name=Oxford>{{cite book
 |title = Oxford Dictionary of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
 |year = 2003
 |publisher = Oxford University Press
 |isbn = 0-19-850673-2
 |url-access = registration
 |url = https://archive.org/details/isbn_9780198506737
 }}</ref>

Chemical derivatives may be used to facilitate analysis. For example, [[melting point]] (MP) analysis can assist in identification of many organic compounds. A crystalline derivative may be prepared, such as a [[semicarbazone]] or [[2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazone]] (derived from [[aldehyde]]s or [[ketone]]s), as a simple way of verifying the identity of the original compound, assuming that a table of derivative MP values is available.<ref name=Williamson>{{cite book
 |last = Williamson
 |first = Kenneth L.
 |title = Macroscale and Microscale Organic Experiments, 3rd ed.
 |publisher = Houghton-Mifflin
 |year = 1999
 |location = Boston
 |pages = 426–7
 |isbn = 0-395-90220-7}}</ref> Prior to the advent of [[spectroscopic analysis]], such methods were widely used.

In [[analytical chemistry]], [[derivatization]] can be used to convert [[Analyte|analytes]] into other species for improving detection. For example, [[Chemical polarity|polar]] groups such as [[Amine|N-H]] or [[Alcohol (chemistry)|O-H]] can be converted into less polar groups. This reaction reduces the [[boiling point]] of the molecule, allowing non-[[Volatility (chemistry)|volatile]] compounds to be analyzed by [[gas chromatography]].<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Jones |first1=Jay |last2=Stenerson |first2=Katherine |title=The Use of Derivatization Reagents for GC |url=https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/ES/es/technical-documents/technical-article/analytical-chemistry/gas-chromatography/the-use-of-derivatization |url-status=live |website=SIgma Aldrich |access-date=2023-05-10 |archive-date=2023-02-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230209104247/https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/ES/es/technical-documents/technical-article/analytical-chemistry/gas-chromatography/the-use-of-derivatization }}</ref>

'''Seyðisfjörður''' ({{IPA|is|ˈseiːðɪsˌfjœrðʏr̥|audio=Seyðisfjörður pronunciation.ogg}}) is a town in the [[Eastern Region (Iceland)|Eastern Region]] of [[Iceland]] at the innermost point of the [[fjord]] of the same name. The town is located in the [[Municipalities of Iceland|municipality]] of [[Múlaþing]] and is notable for its artistic culture and innovation, exemplified by the [[LungA Art Festival]] and [[LungA School]], as well as a vibrant community of local artists, galleries, and cultural events. Seyðisfjörður also serves as the Icelandic port for the [[MS Norröna|Norröna]] ferry, providing a direct connection to mainland Europe via the [[Faroe Islands]] and [[Denmark]].

A road over Fjarðarheiði mountain pass (elevation {{convert|600|m|ft|disp=or|abbr=on}}) connects Seyðisfjörður to the rest of Iceland; {{convert|27|km|mi|frac=2|abbr=off}} to the [[Route 1 (Iceland)|Ring Road]] and [[Egilsstaðir]]. Seyðisfjörður is surrounded by mountains with the most prominent Mt. Bjólfur to the west (1085 m) and Strandartindur (1010 m) to the east. The fjord itself is accessible on each side from the town, by following the main road that leads through the town. Further out the fjord is fairly remote but rich with natural interests including [[Atlantic puffin|puffin]] colonies and ruins of former activity such as nearby [[Vestdalseyri]] {{IPA|is|ˈvɛstˌtalsˌeiːrɪ|}}, from where the local church was transported.

'''''Music Box''''' is the third studio album by American singer-songwriter [[Mariah Carey]]. It was released on August 31, 1993, by [[Columbia Records]]. In an attempt to appeal to a wider audience, Carey sought a radio-friendly approach for ''Music Box''. 

''Music Box'' saw Carey working with both new and returning producers and songwriters, including [[Kenneth "Babyface" Edmonds]], [[Robert Clivillés]], [[Walter Afanasieff]], [[David Cole (music producer)|David Cole]], and [[Daryl Simmons]]. It is a [[pop music|pop]] and [[contemporary R&B|R&B]] album infused with [[soul music|soul]], [[gospel music|gospel]], [[dance music|dance]], and [[jazz]]. ''Music Box'' consists mainly of [[pop ballad]]s and [[uptempo]] dance tracks. Despite the involvement of multiple producers, most of the songwriting was handled by Carey and Afanasieff, who had previously collaborated on ''[[Emotions (Mariah Carey album)|Emotions]]'' (1991), continuing a partnership that would conclude with ''[[Butterfly (Mariah Carey album)|Butterfly]]'' (1997). She also experimented with different production techniques, including a more [[Album#Live|live]]-oriented sound and a more restrained use of her upper [[vocal register|register]].

''Music Box'' was promoted with the North American [[Music Box Tour]]—her debut [[concert tour]]—and five [[single (music)|singles]]. The first two, "[[Dreamlover]]" and "[[Hero (Mariah Carey song)|Hero]]", spent eight and four consecutive weeks at number one on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], respectively. They were nominated for [[Best Female Pop Vocal Performance]] at the [[36th Annual Grammy Awards|36th]] (1994) and [[37th Annual Grammy Awards|37th]] (1995) [[Grammy Awards|Annual Grammy Awards]], respectively. The international third and fourth singles, "[[Without You (Mariah Carey recording)|Without You]]" and "[[Anytime You Need a Friend]]", were commercially successful worldwide; "Without You" became her most successful song globally. In the US, "Without You" and "[[Never Forget You (Mariah Carey song)|Never Forget You]]" were issued as a [[double A-side single]] that reached the top three of the Hot 100.{{efn|"Never Forget You" was issued as a double A-side single with "Without You" exclusively in the United States, and not released as a single anywhere else; the international success of "Without You" occurred independently of "Never Forget You". Consequently, "Anytime You Need a Friend" was the fifth single from ''Music Box'' in the United States, but the fourth internationally.}}

On release, ''Music Box'' received generally mixed reviews from [[music critic]]s, who praised Carey's vocal performance and some of the songs but criticized its mellow, formulaic, and subdued lyricism. Retrospective reviews have been more positive; many have underscored its significance in her career. The album topped the charts in 17 countries, including Australia, France, Germany, and the United Kingdom. In the United States, it topped the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]] for eight non-consecutive weeks and was certified [[RIAA certification|diamond]] by the [[Recording Industry Association of America]]. ''Music Box'' remains Carey's bestseller and one of the [[List of best-selling albums|best-selling albums of all time]], with over 30 million copies sold worldwide.

{{Short description|Creation and selling of music}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=December 2022}}

[[File:MCI equipped Studiod.jpg|thumb|Musicians working in a [[recording studio]] in 2010]]
[[File:Crowd watching The Proclaimers, Towersey 2018.jpg|thumb|An audience watching [[w:The Proclaimers|The Proclaimers]] at [[w:Towersey Festival|Towersey Festival]], 2018]]
The '''music industry''' are individuals and organizations that earn money by [[Songwriter|writing songs]] and [[musical composition]]s, creating and selling [[Sound recording and reproduction|recorded music]] and [[sheet music]], presenting [[live music|concerts]], as well as the organizations that aid, train, represent and supply [[music]] creators. Among the many individuals and organizations that operate in the industry are: the songwriters and [[composer]]s who write songs and musical compositions; the [[singer]]s, [[musician]]s, [[Conducting|conductors]], and [[bandleader]]s who perform the music; the [[record label]]s, [[music publisher]]s, [[recording studio]]s, [[Record producer|music producers]], [[audio engineer]]s, [[Record shop|retail]] and [[digital music store]]s, and [[Performance rights organisation|performance rights organizations]] who create and sell recorded music and sheet music; and the [[talent agent|booking agents]], [[Promoter (entertainment)|promoters]], [[music venue]]s, [[road crew]], and audio engineers who help organize and sell concerts.

The industry also includes a range of professionals who assist singers and musicians with their music careers. These include [[talent manager]]s, [[artists and repertoire]] managers, [[business manager]]s, [[entertainment law]]yers; those who broadcast audio or video music content ([[Satellite radio|satellite]], [[Internet radio]] stations, [[Radio broadcasting|broadcast radio]] and [[Television broadcaster|TV stations]]); [[music journalist]]s and [[Music criticism|music critics]]; [[DJ]]s; [[music education|music educators and teachers]]; manufacturers of [[musical instrument]]s and music equipment; as well as many others. In addition to the businesses and artists there are organizations that also play an important role, including musician's unions (e.g. [[American Federation of Musicians]]), not-for-profit performance-rights organizations (e.g. [[American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers]]) and other associations (e.g. [[International Alliance for Women in Music]], a non-profit organization that advocates for [[Women in music|women composers and musicians]]).

The modern Western music industry emerged between the 1930s and 1950s, when [[Phonograph record|records]] replaced [[sheet music]] as the most important product in the music business. In the commercial world, "the recording industry"—a reference to [[sound recording|recording performances of songs and pieces]] and selling the recordings–began to be used as a loose synonym for "the music industry". By the 2020s, a majority of the music market is controlled by four major corporate labels: the French-owned [[Universal Music Group]], the Japanese-owned [[Sony Music Group]],<ref name="sonybmg">Sony Corporation announced October 1, 2008, that it had completed the acquisition of Bertelsmann's 50% stake in Sony BMG, which was originally announced on August 5, 2008. Ref: {{cite press release|url=http://www.sony.com/SCA/press/081001.shtml|title=Sony's acquisition of Bertelsmann's 50% Stake in Sony BMG complete.|publisher=Sony Corporation of America|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081003004815/http://www.sony.com/SCA/press/081001.shtml|archive-date=October 3, 2008}}</ref> the American-owned [[Warner Music Group]], and the German/American-owned [[BMG Rights Management]]. Labels outside of these three major labels are referred to as [[independent label]]s (or "indies"), such as [[Allied Artists Music Group]], [[Reservoir Media]], [[Secretly Group]], [[Big Machine Records|Big Machine Label Group]], [[PIAS Group]], [[Beggars Group]], [[Sub Pop]], [[Domino Recording Company]], [[Glassnote Records]], [[Ninja Tune]], [[Empire Distribution]], & [[ECR Music Group]]. The largest portion of the live music market for concerts and tours is controlled by [[Live Nation]], the largest promoter and [[music venue]] owner. Live Nation is a former subsidiary of [[iHeartMedia|iHeartMedia Inc]], which is the largest owner of radio stations in the [[United States]].

In the first decades of the 21st century, the music industry underwent drastic changes with the advent of widespread digital distribution of music via the [[Internet]] (which includes both illegal [[file sharing]] of songs and legal music purchases in [[online music store]]s). A conspicuous indicator of these changes is total music sales: since the year 2000, sales of recorded music have dropped off substantially,<ref>{{cite news | title=The Music Industry | url=http://www.economist.com/background/displayBackground.cfm?story_id=10498664 | date=October 15, 2008 | newspaper=The Economist | access-date=December 2, 2008 | archive-date=June 29, 2011 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110629203652/http://www.economist.com/background/displayBackground.cfm?story_id=10498664 | url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="CNN">{{cite web | last=Goldman| first=David| date=February 3, 2010| title=Music's lost decade: Sales cut in half|work = CNN Money| url-status=dead| archive-date=June 27, 2020| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20200627183249/https://money.cnn.com/2010/02/02/news/companies/napster_music_industry/ | url=https://money.cnn.com/2010/02/02/news/companies/napster_music_industry/}}</ref> while, in contrast, [[live music]] has increased in importance.<ref name="Live Nation">{{cite magazine | last = Seabrook | first = John | author-link = John Seabrook | title = The Price of the Ticket | series = Annals of Entertainment | date = August 10, 2009 | magazine = [[The New Yorker]] | url = https://www.newyorker.com/reporting/2009/08/10/090810fa_fact_seabrook | page = 34 | access-date = February 20, 2020 | archive-date = October 21, 2013 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20131021050008/http://www.newyorker.com/reporting/2009/08/10/090810fa_fact_seabrook | url-status = live }}</ref> In 2011, the largest recorded music retailer in the world was now a digital, Internet-based platform operated by a computer company: [[Apple Inc.]]'s online [[iTunes Store]].<ref>{{cite news | url = http://www.dailywireless.org/2011/02/14/mobile-world-congress-2011/ | title = Mobile World Congress 2011 | quote = "Amazon is now the world's biggest book retailer. Apple, the world's largest music retailer." | work = dailywireless.org | date = February 14, 2011 | access-date = February 28, 2011 | archive-date = October 21, 2013 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20131021070502/http://www.dailywireless.org/2011/02/14/mobile-world-congress-2011/ | url-status = dead }}</ref> Since 2011, the music industry has seen consistent growth, with streaming now generating more revenue per year than digital downloads. [[Spotify]], [[Apple Music]], and [[Amazon Music]] are the largest streaming services by subscriber count.<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Lee|first1=Tyler|last2=PDT|first2=on 4 May 2020 15:51 |title=Spotify Was The Largest Music Streaming Service For 2019|url=https://www.ubergizmo.com/2020/04/spotify-largest-music-streaming-service-2019/ |access-date= March 3, 2021|website=Ubergizmo|language=en-US|archive-date=February 5, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210205081059/https://www.ubergizmo.com/2020/04/spotify-largest-music-streaming-service-2019/ |url-status=live}}</ref> In addition to streaming services, the development and success of social media platforms, especially [[TikTok]], have also contributed to this dramatic increase in revenue and dictated the trends of the industry.

{{short description|Literature written during the English restoration}}
[[File:Charles II of England in Coronation robes.jpg|thumb|right|upright=1.2|The [[English monarchy]] was restored when [[Charles II of England]] (above) became king in 1660.]]
'''Restoration literature''' is the [[English literature]] written during the historical period commonly referred to as the [[Stuart Restoration|English Restoration]] (1660–1688), which corresponds to the last years of [[Stuart period|Stuart reign]] in England, Scotland, [[Wales]], and Ireland. In general, the term is used to denote roughly homogeneous styles of literature that centre on a celebration of or reaction to the restored court of [[Charles II of England|Charles II]]. It is a literature that includes extremes, for it encompasses both ''[[Paradise Lost]]'' and the [[John Wilmot, 2nd Earl of Rochester|Earl of Rochester]]'s ''[[Sodom, or the Quintessence of Debauchery|Sodom]]'', the high-spirited [[Sex comedy|sexual comedy]] of ''[[The Country Wife]]'' and the moral wisdom of ''[[The Pilgrim's Progress]]''. It saw [[John Locke|Locke]]'s ''[[Two Treatises of Government|Treatises of Government]]'', the founding of the [[Royal Society]], the experiments and holy meditations of [[Robert Boyle]], the hysterical attacks on theatres from [[Jeremy Collier]], and the pioneering of [[literary criticism]] from [[John Dryden]] and [[John Dennis (dramatist)|John Dennis]]. The period witnessed news becoming a commodity, the [[essay]] developing into a periodical art form, and the beginnings of [[textual criticism]].

The dates for Restoration literature are  a matter of convention, and they differ markedly from [[literary genre|genre]] to genre. Thus, the "Restoration" in [[English drama|drama]] may last until 1700, while in [[English poetry|poetry]] it may last only until 1666 (see [[1666 in poetry]]) and the ''[[annus mirabilis]]''; and in prose it might end in 1688, with the increasing tensions over succession and the corresponding rise in [[journalism]] and [[magazine|periodicals]], or not until 1700, when those periodicals grew more stabilized. In general, scholars use the term "Restoration"  to denote the literature that began and flourished under Charles II, whether that literature was the laudatory [[ode]] that gained a new life with restored aristocracy, the [[eschatology|eschatological]] literature that showed an increasing despair among [[Puritan]]s, or the literature of rapid communication and trade that followed in the wake of England's mercantile empire.

[[File:charles-pineapple.jpg|thumb|right|Charles II being given the first [[pineapple]] grown in England by his gardener, John Rose; note also the [[Cavalier King Charles Spaniel]]s in the foreground]]

{{Short description|Organic compounds that contain sulfur}}
'''Organosulfur chemistry''' is the study of the properties and synthesis of '''organosulfur compounds''', which are [[organic compound]]s that contain [[sulfur]].<ref>{{cite book|last=Block|first=E.|title=Reactions of Organosulfur Compounds|publisher=Academic Press|year=1978|isbn=0-12-107050-6}}</ref> They are often associated with foul odors, but many of the sweetest compounds known are organosulfur derivatives, e.g., [[saccharin]]. Nature abounds with organosulfur compounds—sulfur is vital for life. Of the 20 common [[amino acids]], two ([[cysteine]] and [[methionine]]) are organosulfur compounds, and the antibiotics [[penicillin]] and [[sulfa drugs]] both contain sulfur. While sulfur-containing antibiotics save many lives, [[sulfur mustard]] is a deadly chemical warfare agent. [[Fossil fuels]], [[coal]], [[petroleum]], and [[natural gas]], which are derived from ancient organisms, necessarily contain organosulfur compounds, [[Desulfurization|the removal]] of which is a [[Claus process|major focus]] of [[oil refineries]].

Sulfur shares the [[chalcogen]] group with [[oxygen]], [[selenium]], and [[tellurium]], and it is expected that organosulfur compounds have similarities with carbon–oxygen, carbon–selenium, and carbon–tellurium compounds.

A classical [[chemical test]] for the detection of sulfur compounds is the [[Carius halogen method]].

{{Short description|Method of network communication where requests are sent by the publisher}}
'''Push technology,''' also known as '''server push,''' is a communication method where the communication is initiated by a [[Server (computing)|server]] rather than a [[Client (computing)|client]]. This approach is different from the "[[Pull technology|pull]]" method where the communication is initiated by a client.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2012-11-18 |title=Push Technology |url=https://www.techopedia.com/definition/5732/push-technology |access-date=2023-07-23 |website=Techopedia |language=en-US}}</ref>

In push technology, clients can express their preferences for certain types of information or data, typically through a process known as the [[Publish–subscribe pattern|publish–subscribe]] model. In this model, a client "subscribes" to specific information channels hosted by a server. When new content becomes available on these channels, the server automatically sends, or "pushes," this information to the subscribed client.

Under certain conditions, such as restrictive security policies that block incoming [[HTTP]] requests, push technology is sometimes simulated using a technique called [[Polling (computer science)|polling.]] In these cases, the client periodically checks with the server to see if new information is available, rather than receiving automatic updates.

{{Short description|Behaviour that increases the fitness of another while decreasing the fitness of self}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=February 2015}}
[[File:Grooming monkeys.jpg|thumb|An [[olive baboon]] [[social grooming|allogrooming]] a younger one]]

In [[biology]], '''altruism''' is behaviour by an individual that increases the [[fitness (biology)|fitness]] of another individual while decreasing their own.<ref name="Bell_2008">{{cite book |vauthors=Bell G |title=Selection: The Mechanism of Evolution |url=https://archive.org/details/selectionmechani00bell_664 |url-access=limited | year=2008 |publisher=[[Oxford University Press]] | location=Oxford |isbn=978-0-19-856972-5 |pages=[https://archive.org/details/selectionmechani00bell_664/page/n381 367]–368}}</ref> [[Altruism]] in this sense differs from the philosophical concept of [[altruism (ethics)|altruism]], in which an action would only be called "altruistic" if it was done with the conscious intention of helping another. In the behavioural sense, there is no such requirement. As such, it is not evaluated in moral terms; it is the consequences of an action for reproductive fitness that determine whether the action is considered altruistic, not the intentions, if any, with which the action is performed.<ref name="Okasha_2008">{{cite encyclopedia |url=https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/altruism-biological |title=Biological altruism |vauthors=Okasha S |encyclopedia=[[Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy]] |year=2008 |access-date=2013-07-20}}</ref>

The term ''altruism'' was coined by the French philosopher [[Auguste Comte]] in French, as ''altruisme'', for an [[antonym]] of [[egoism]].<ref>{{OEtymD |altruism |access-date=2014-09-19}}</ref><ref>{{cite book | vauthors = Teske N |title=Political Activists in America: The Identity Construction Model of Political Participation |date=2009 |publisher=[[Penn State University Press]] |location=[[Pennsylvania State University|University Park, PA]] |isbn=978-0-271-03546-8 |page=101 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7B38I2UEPa0C}}</ref> He derived it from the Italian ''altrui'', which in turn was derived from Latin ''alteri'', meaning "other people" or "somebody else".<ref>{{cite book | vauthors=Ciciloni F |title=A Grammar of the Italian Language |year=1825 |publisher=[[John Murray (publishing house)|John Murray]] |location=London |page=[https://archive.org/details/agrammaritalian00cicigoog/page/n81 64] |url=https://archive.org/details/agrammaritalian00cicigoog |isbn=}}</ref>

Altruistic behaviours appear most obviously in [[kin selection|kin relationships]], such as in parenting, but may also be evident among wider social groups, such as in social insects. They allow an individual to increase the success of its genes by helping relatives that share those genes.<ref name="Davies_2012">{{cite book |vauthors=Davies NB, Krebs JR, West SA |title=An Introduction to Behavioural Ecology |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=G9mXO5asWi8C |date= 2012-04-09 |publisher=[[Wiley (publisher)|John Wiley & Sons]] |isbn=978-1-4443-3949-9 |pages=307–333 |chapter=11}}</ref>

Obligate altruism is the permanent loss of direct fitness (with potential for indirect fitness gain).<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Galliard|first1=Jean-François Le |last2=Ferriére|first2=Regis |last3=Dieckmann|first3=Ulf |year=2003 |title=The Adaptive Dynamics of Altruism in Spatially Heterogeneous Populations |journal=[[Evolution (journal)|Evolution]] |volume=57 |issue=1 |pages=1–17 |doi=10.1111/j.0014-3820.2003.tb00211.x |pmid=12643563 |s2cid=13266199 |issn=1558-5646 |doi-access=free}}</ref> For example, [[honey bee]] [[worker bee|workers]] may forage for the colony. Facultative altruism is temporary loss of direct fitness (with potential for indirect fitness gain followed by personal reproduction). For example, a [[Florida scrub jay]] may help at the nest, then gain parental territory.<ref>{{cite book |title=Animal Behavior |vauthors=Alcock A |edition=9th |publisher=[[Sinauer Associates]] |year=2009 |isbn=978-0-87893-225-2}}</ref>
